title: The Educated Barbarian: Hagakure analysis (part. 21)
summary: Penultimate Hagakure episode. NH discusses raising hunting dogs, strict upbringing of boys and girls, accepting inevitable ruin, the law of attraction and sincerity, and remembering your roots, which he ties to bodybuilding motivation and teaching. Stoicism comes next.
claims: Feeding a hunting puppy boar meat mirrors the bodybuilder belief that you are what you eat
Japan kept hunting dogs without affection, so the hunt took priority if one died; some cultures still do this
Modern parenting makes the child royalty and parents servants; kids need structure and schedules, and lack of rigidity harms them more than an occasional spank
Starving a lazy child for a day is too extreme, but today's parents are too sweet
When something has crumbled beyond saving, accept it immediately and move on rather than whining; prevent the ruin if you still can
Societal upheaval may come, and some people already have plans for the reset; people must take charge of their own lives afterward
He disagrees with imposing virtue rules on girls; men and women should be free to choose, including choosing to be a homemaker
Westerners who call these rules barbaric yet excuse them in other cultures are hypocrites
Imposing gendered molds on children either doubles down on their nature or shackles their uniqueness
The law of attraction existed in Japan 500 years ago; you attract what you manifest, negativity draws negative people
Positive people repel negative vampires, who either try to drag you down, get saved, or flee
Be sincere and yourself; faking a persona takes effort and a person who never lies doesn't have to remember what they said
Bodybuilders who make it often forget where they came from; remembering your weak past makes you a relatable teacher and keeps you motivated
